scenario.story: Your team has three hits. Can you find the smallest upgrade that changes the matchup?
scenario.information: A game-inspired training simulation. Values and upgrade rules are supplied practice data, not live Brawl Stars stats. Assume every hit lands, with no healing or other modifiers.

tasks.title: Reconstruct the health bar
tasks.intro: Two unshielded hits each deal {{hit}} damage. The target has {{remaining}} health left. Reconstruct its starting health h.
hints: How much health did the two unshielded hits remove?
Combine the two hit amounts before isolating h.
Add the health lost from both hits to both sides.
tasks.takeaway: An equation lets you reconstruct a quantity you could not observe directly.

tasks.title: Find what the shield removes
tasks.intro: A raw hit of {{raw}} deals {{actual}} through the shield. Find the fraction r removed.
hints: The fraction 1 − r tells you how much gets through.
Divide both sides by the raw damage, or distribute first.
After dividing, subtract 1, then divide by −1.
tasks.takeaway: A reduction of 1/5 means 20% is removed and 80% gets through.

tasks.title: Turn the formula around
tasks.intro: Our practice upgrades start at {{base}} raw damage and add {{gain}} per upgrade. Isolate u in terms of desired damage d.
hints: Keep d as a variable. Build a reusable formula.
Subtract the starting damage from both sides.
Divide the entire remaining expression by the damage gained per upgrade.
tasks.takeaway: The same relationship can answer “how much damage?” or “how many upgrades?”

tasks.title: Find the upgrade that matters
tasks.intro: Combine the published health and shield results. Find raw damage d so three hits cover the target’s health, then use the upgrade formula. Only whole upgrades can be bought.
hints: Use the health and shield results to find raw damage first.
Three hits deliver 3 × 0.8 × d damage. Divide the health by 2.4.
Put that damage into u = (d − 1800)/200. If it is fractional, test the next whole upgrade and the one below.
tasks.takeaway: A threshold can make one small upgrade change the number of hits needed.

tasks.title: Take the idea with you
tasks.intro: A new relationship, without the game data: solve for x. Explain one operation you used. Your work is saved separately from your teammates’ checks.
hints: There are x terms on both sides. Preserve equality as you collect them.
Distribute 4 to both terms inside the parentheses.
Subtract 2x from both sides, add 12, then divide by 2.
tasks.takeaway: You can carry the same algebraic moves into a new situation.
